title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page appears to be scratch work in the genus-0 part of the Teichmüller-groupoid notes. It seems to be looking for natural base points in M_{0,5}, namely points with nontrivial automorphism group, as Grothendieck does for M_{0,4} with the harmonic and equianharmonic points. Two readings are offered; the first is better supported by the page.

Left column: three configurations of 5 points on the Riemann sphere, each drawn with the label of its symmetry group.
(i) Regular pentagon on a great circle. The holomorphic automorphisms preserving the set form D5 (order 10). The rotations preserving an orientation of the circle form Z/5 (the arrow Z/5 -> D5). Adding the reflection in the equatorial plane (the anti-holomorphic or 'non-oriented' theory) gives D5 x Z/2 (order 20).
(ii) Square pyramid: four points on the equator plus one pole. Holomorphic symmetry Z/4; with reflections C4v ≅ D4. The image reads Z/4Z, not Z/2Z.
(iii) Triangular bipyramid: three equatorial points plus two poles. Holomorphic symmetry D3 = S3, with Z/3 the part preserving the orientation of the equatorial circle. With reflections, D3h = S3 x Z/2.

Right column: Grothendieck counts how many labelled configurations (points of M_{0,5} with ordered marked points) of each type exist. The word K seems to denote the circle (cycle) through the points, which can be oriented.
- Pentagon: 12 = number of cyclic orders of 5 labels up to reversal. Equivalently 120/|D5| = 120/10 = 12.
- Square pyramid: 30 = 15 x 2. Choose the pole (5 ways), then a cyclic order of the 4 others up to reversal (3 ways), giving 15. Then double, because the stabilizer does not contain an orientation-reversing element of the circle K ('n'implique pas orientation de K'). Equivalently 120/|Z/4| = 30.
- Bipyramid: 20 = 10 x 2. Choose the 2 poles (10 ways), then double for the orientation of K. Equivalently 120/|S3| = 20.

In each case ('NB') he observes that the numbers are those of the icosahedron: 12 vertices, 30 edges, 20 faces. The stabilizers in the rotation group A5 are Z/5, Z/2, Z/3. In A5 x Z/2 they are D5, D2 = Z/2 x Z/2, S3. So the S5-orbits of the special points of M_{0,5}, and their stabilizers, are compared with the A5-orbits of vertices, edges and faces of the icosahedron. In both the oriented and the non-oriented theory, the icosahedral stabilizers sit with index 2 inside the M_{0,5} stabilizers: Z/5 ⊂ D5, Z/2 ⊂ Z/4, Z/3 ⊂ S3, and D5 ⊂ D5 x Z/2, D2 ⊂ D4, S3 ⊂ S3 x Z/2.

Top sketches: a triangle labelled 0, 1, ∞ with a hemisphere P_+, a bipyramid with shaded triangles, and a bow-tie graph. These point to the dessin / barycentric-triangle viewpoint. In that viewpoint the icosahedron is the regular map over P^1 branched at 0, 1, ∞, with 12, 30, 20 points over 0, 1, ∞. The 'non-oriented' version uses flags, i.e. the triangles P_+ and P_-.

The next page goes on to the formalism of tangential base points ('points base à l'infini'). This page is a preliminary inventory of the 'finite' base points of M_{0,5} with automorphisms.
errors: The numerical coincidence with the icosahedron is not an identification of stabilizers. The S5-stabilizers of the special points of M_{0,5} (D5, Z/4, S3) are twice the size of the A5 icosahedral stabilizers (Z/5, Z/2, Z/3). Also Z/4 is not D2, so the non-oriented groups D4 and D2 differ in type. Grothendieck seems aware of this (index-2 arrows, 'x2'), but the page does not explain the correspondence.

Some phrases on the right side contradict the left column. On the right he gives D5 for the vertex stabilizer in the non-oriented case; on the left he gives D5 x Z/2. This is consistent only if the right side refers to the icosahedron (A5 x Z/2) and the left to M_{0,5} (S5 x conjugation). That is plausible, but the writing is ambiguous and contains crossed-out attempts.

ideas.what: Classification of 5-point configurations on P^1 with nontrivial symmetry (pentagon, square pyramid, triangular bipyramid) as special points / orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S5, in holomorphic and anti-holomorphic versions
ideas.modern_name: orbifold (elliptic) points of M_{0,5}/S5; S5 x Gal(C/R)-stabilizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (finite subgroups of PGL2; point configurations); folklore in the moduli literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points with automorphisms for M_{0,4} and the role of M_{0,5}; this explicit list is not known to me there

ideas.what: Counting the S5-orbits of these points: 12, 30, 20 (via cyclic orders on an oriented circle K), and noting the coincidence with the vertices, edges and faces of the icosahedron, with comparison of stabilizers in A5 and A5 x Z/2
ideas.modern_name: orbit-stabilizer count; A5 regular map (icosahedral dessin) vs S5 action on M_{0,5}
ideas.usually_credited_to: counts are elementary; the A5/S5 symmetry of the quintic del Pezzo M̄_{0,5} is classical

ideas.what: Oriented vs non-oriented theory (adjoining complex conjugation / reflections) throughout the base-point inventory
ideas.modern_name: real structure; action of Gal(C/R) on Teichmüller groupoids; cartographic group vs oriented cartographic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (dessins, Esquisse); later Schneps et al.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (oriented / non-oriented cartographic groups)

missed.claim: Grothendieck notices that the S5-orbits of special points of M_{0,5} have sizes 12, 30, 20, matching the icosahedron's vertices, edges and faces, with stabilizers related by index 2. He hints at a correspondence (via the orientation of the circle K) but does not make it explicit. No geometric explanation is given on the page.
missed.quote: CNB 12 sommets de l'icos. le stabilisateur d'un sommet est Z/5Z ... 30 = 15 × 2 possibilités ... 20 = 10 × 2 possibilités
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small curiosity in the combinatorics of base points for the genus-0, n=5 Teichmüller groupoid. It probably follows from known A5/S5 geometry of the quintic del Pezzo surface and is unlikely to be new.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary symmetry counts of special points of M_{0,5}, compared with the icosahedron. The material is routine and the comparison is suggestive but undeveloped, so it is a minor unpublished detail at most.
